Node N3, the running pump leg, row by row

Worked example

File ▸ Worked example fills node N3 only

Interactive · build a deviation

Guide word plus parameter gives a deviation to test

Seven parameters × eleven guide words on N3; the team keeps the nine pairs with a credible cause.

Worksheet order

Write the consequence before you credit any safeguard

1 · Deviation

Flow NO: pump against a blocked discharge.

2 · Causes

V201 closed in the field; V100 closed.

3 · Consequences

Casing heats 6 °C/min; seal fails; gas oil released.

4 · Safeguards

TSHH-212 trip; TI-212, FRC-100 alarms.

5 · S, L, risk

S4 × L3 = 12, High.

6 · Actions

R11 recycle, R12 low-flow trip, R24 alarm.

Step 3 assumes no protection works; step 5 counts it.

Interactive · rank the risk

Risk = S × L, read against four bands

Bands: 1–4 Low, 5–9 Medium, 10–16 High, 20–25 Very high. A High row needs a recommendation and is a LOPA candidate.

Simulator link

A green ▶ OTS chip runs the deviation on the DCS console

    Watch which alarm comes first and how long the operator has; then judge the safeguards column again.

    Step 5 · Actions

    One recommendation list, linked to every row it closes

    • Each has an owner, a due date and a status.
    • Edit once: Global changes every row, Local one row.
    • Open points go to the Parking Lot.

    Part 3 · LOPA, report, hand-in

    How does the Full edition rate a scenario with LOPA, and how do we hand in?

    Part 3 · the plan

    From a ranked row to a number, then to a report

    1. LOPA symbolsfrequency, PFD and the tolerable target
    2. The equationsf_unmit, f_mit, RRR and RRF, step by step
    3. Scenario groupswhy the sum matters
    4. Check, report, hand inand the projector workshop

    Full edition · LOPA columns

    Five quantities turn a row into a frequencystep 1 of 3

    S × L ranks a row; LOPA asks whether its frequency is low enough.

    $f_{IE}$
    initiating-event frequency of one cause
    1/yr
    $P_{en}$, $P_{cm}$
    enabling condition, conditional modifier (ignition, occupancy)
    –
    $PFD_j$
    failure on demand of IPL $j$: independent, specific, auditable
    –
    $TEL$
    tolerable frequency for the row's severity S
    1/yr

    PHA Studio's library values are CCPS-style teaching defaults; edit them under Project ▸ LOPA Data.

    Full edition · scenario dialog

    Multiply down the layers, then comparestep 2 of 3

    $f_{unmit}=\sum f_{IE}\times\prod P_{en}\times\prod P_{cm}$how often the hazard is reached with no IPL
    $f_{mit}=f_{unmit}\times\prod_j PFD_j$each IPL must fail too
    $RRR=\dfrac{TEL}{f_{mit}},\qquad RRF=\dfrac{f_{mit}}{TEL}$PFD an extra layer must reach; factor still missing

    Both read “None” when $f_{mit}\le TEL$: the row meets its target.

    Worked example · N3 Flow NO, deadhead

    One cause, one IPL, one numberstep 3 of 3

    From step 2$f_{mit}=\sum f_{IE}\prod P_{en}\prod P_{cm}\prod PFD_j,\quad RRF=f_{mit}/TEL$
    $f_{unmit}=0.1\times0.1=1\times10^{-2}\ \text{/yr}$V201 closed in the field × ignition
    $f_{mit}=10^{-2}\times0.007=7\times10^{-5}\ \text{/yr}$TSHH-212 trip credited
    $TEL(S4)=10^{-3}\ \Rightarrow\ f_{mit}\le TEL$RRR, RRF: None

    TI-212 HI is not credited: it shares TE-212 with the trip, so it is not independent.

    Interactive · LOPA calculator

    Move a factor and watch the gap to the target

    LOPA$f_{mit}=f_{IE}\,P_{cm}\,PFD,\ \ RRF=f_{mit}/TEL$

    At the N3 values (0.1, 0.1, 0.007, S4) the bar sits below TEL, as in PHA Studio's scenario dialog.

    Full edition

    The scenario dialog shows every step of the sum

    • Turn on Show LOPA columns in the worksheet.
    • Pick IPLs from the row's linked safeguards.
    • Red cell: gap. Green: meets. Yellow: no S yet.

    Interactive · Scenario Groups

    Rows that end in the same harm add up

    Group$f_{group}=\sum_i f_{mit,i}\ \le\ TEL$

    Causes from the LOPA tab, scenario L1, each with ignition 0.1 and TSHH-212 credited: one row meets TEL, the group may not.

    Step 6 · Check and report

    Data check first, then the report writes itself

    • Data check: rows without S, L, safeguard or owner.
    • Report: print, Word, HTML, Excel, CSV.
    • File ▸ Save a .json and hand it in with the Excel.

    On the projector

    Workshop mode walks parameter × guide word with a timer

    • One deviation per screen, large type.
    • Phones send ideas by QR code.
    • Phone ideas need an http(s) copy, such as GitHub Pages.

    Part 3 · summary

    What part 3 settled

    • $f_{mit}$ multiplies frequency by every failure.
    • N3 deadhead: 7 × 10⁻⁵ /yr below TEL 10⁻³.
    • Credit only independent layers.
    • Groups sum rows with one harm.
    • Check, report, save, hand in.

    This deck

    Key Takeaways

    1

    Study one node at a time, against its design intent.

    2

    Write the consequence before crediting any safeguard.

    3

    Run the deviation on the OTS before you judge the safeguards.

    4

    Credit only independent layers; compare f_mit with TEL.

    5

    Save the .json and hand in the Excel report.
